newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Mouskouri seeks way out for translation plan.
newsitem.headline: Mouskouri seeks way out for translation plan.

text.p: Greek singer Nana Mouskouri will urge the European Parliament on October 21 to find a way round Britain's veto of a European Union programme to help translate books written in lesser-known EU languages.
"We want this programme implemented. We don't want to waste any more time," an assistant for Mouskouri, who became a Euro-MP in 1994, told Reuters on Tuesday.

Last year Britain single-handedly blocked the 34-million-Ecu Ariane programme, which would provide EU money to promote the reading, translation and distribution of books and plays in languages like Welsh, Basque and Gaelic.
Britain said at the time that the scheme concentrated too much on translating and would be a waste of money.

Mouskouri, who will be presenting her report on Ariane to the parliament on October 21, will urge fellow Euro-MPs to accept parts of a provisional compromise hammered out by the Culture Council on July 15.
Ministers have to agree the programme, COM(94)356, unanimously and win the support of the 626-member parliament to push the programme through.

The Council's compromise entails cutting the programme from five to two years but widening its scope to fund other activities, such as joint projects by publishers from different countries to promote little-known but promising works of literature.

But even if the assembly agrees to these changes, there may still be problems in breaking the deadlock because deputies are unlikely to accept the ministers' proposal to axe the Ariane budget to seven million Ecus, a fivefold drop.
Mouskouri believes 10.5 million Ecus is the minimum acceptable.
